assessment: The short exact sequence is already stated clearly, so missing art alone is not a defect. A small commutative/exactness schematic would be a useful optional supplement if it explicitly ties the map from the ordered-cover fundamental group to the unordered-cover fundamental group and the endpoint monodromy to S_n, with injectivity, kernel=image, and surjectivity annotations.

mathematical_checks.sequence_order: 1 -> PB_n -> B_n^conf -> S_n -> 1, matching the source.
mathematical_checks.p_star: p_* maps PB_n = pi_1(F_n(D^2),q) to B_n^conf = pi_1(C_n(D^2),[q]) by the quotient p; the source correctly claims it is injective because p is a covering.
mathematical_checks.endpoint_monodromy: pi maps B_n^conf to S_n. For a loop class [alpha], its lift starting at q ends at sigma_alpha dot q and pi([alpha])=sigma_alpha; this is the stated map direction and convention.
mathematical_checks.exactness: The proof establishes im(p_*)=ker(pi): a lifted loop has identity monodromy exactly when it closes at q. It separately establishes surjectivity of pi by realizing adjacent transpositions and using that they generate S_n; p_* is injective.
mathematical_checks.edge_cases: For n=0 and n=1 the source identifies PB_n, B_n^conf, and S_n as trivial groups, so the sequence reduces to the exact sequence of one-element groups.
mathematical_checks.conventions: The proof uses the first-then-second loop product and defines monodromy by the permutation sigma satisfying endpoint=sigma dot q. No splitting, Artin presentation, or strand-diagram identification is asserted.
